summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The selected scenario is the monolithic 3-D NAND gate without heat extraction, from Fig. 4A-B of W2793410136. It was modeled in COMSOL FEM with steady-state and transient solves. The paper's peak top-tier value is about 420 K, a ~120 K rise over a 300 K sink. The introduction separately cites up to 450 K, and the paper does not say which setup gives it. The gate blocked simulation because the custom experiment has an empty floorplan and no power_w object, so input validity failed (input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false). Only the custom_2d_steady kind was attempted, so no transient trace exists, and independent verification is absent. Not a bundled EV6/GCC run, and no Ascend910 or ATPlace sizes or powers are pinned, so no illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace was generated; no source commit or placement assumption applies. The packet has no pinned assets, and the only link is the COMSOL commercial website. comparison_valid is false, so no numerical comparison to 420 K or 450 K is made. Qualitatively, the paper attributes the hotspot to top-tier heating far from the sink, with the two tiers joined by 50 nm inter-tier vias. A 2D model cannot represent that vertical structure. Mismatches that block comparison: a nanoscale 3-D stack (183x145 nm^2 footprint, 1.4 um height) versus a 2D floorplan with watt-level blocks; peak temperature at the top-tier transistor versus any Studio aggregation; steady-state and 50% duty-cycle transient regimes with results only in figures; boundary conditions of a 300 K isothermal sink face with adiabatic sides versus package cooling; and missing block geometry, per-block watts, and COMSOL model files. This result is a screening outcome only, not a replication of the paper.

Nanoscale device-level 3-D FEM (183x145 nm^2 NAND gate, 1.4 um stack) differs in scale from a centimeter-scale 2D floorplan with watt-level block power. It has no block floorplan and no per-block watts; heat comes from transistor I-V Joule heating at the drain and gate blocks. The scenario is not steady_2d_relevant.

Monolithic 3-D stacking: two tiers joined by 50 nm inter-tier vias, with top-tier heating far from the sink. A 2D Studio model cannot represent this vertical tier structure, which is the cause of the hotspot.
No interposer or chiplet system, and no cooling model beyond a 300 K isothermal sink face with adiabatic sides. This differs from package-level heat-sink or cooling models.

Transient behavior is a 50% duty cycle over 100 ns. The scenario has no published power time series, and the paper's transient results are shown only in figures (Figs. 6-7), not as extractable numbers.
The paper's own heat extraction (thermal junction and tungsten pillar) is a design feature, not a controller or optimizer. It is outside the scenario and cannot be reproduced in a 2D Studio runner.
No reliability model. The paper discusses reliability only qualitatively. Nanoscale conductivity reduction (Si nanowire 13 W/m/K) and quantum effects are simplified or ignored.
No Studio package or material assumptions are recorded here, because the packet has no pinned assets and no Studio bundle specification.

Dimensions and powers do not support a placement. A separate illustrative 2D placement could be constructed only if the runner has dimensions and powers; its coordinates would be generated, not paper-derived, and its temperatures could not be compared numerically to the paper's 420 K.
